# **Introduction**

The main aim of this guide is to provide an understanding about the ~~inheritance~~ breeding system and the strategies involved for creating optimal parent Umas for breeding.

&nbsp;

**Sources:** My sources are mainly from myself, otherwise, sources will be cited if it is externally obtained, example: [Aoneko uma](https://twitter.com/aoneko_uma) & other crowd sourced sites.

&nbsp;

**Prerequisites & Expectations**

This guide is written with the assumption that you **already** know the basics about the game. If anything is foreign to you, you may not be ready for this guide.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**While** Parent farming is not strictly mandatory for the game, it does significantly enhance your runs. Think of it as an optional meta-progression roguelike feature. You are the one to decide for yourself how far/deep you want to delve into the parenting mines.

# **Chapter 1: Compatibility & Inheritance effects**

When starting a run, **both** your parents' overall compatibility score will be displayed using the ◎ / 〇 / △ symbols.

**Overall Compatibility**&nbsp;

◎ Great compatibility (\>150 points)

〇 Good compatibility  (51 – 150 points)

△ Poor compatibility ( \<50 points)

&nbsp;

This overall compatibility is calculated based on the relationship of **all** parents & grandparents with your target horse, added with the total number of overlapping races that each of them has run.

&nbsp;

However, the exact compatibility numbers are hidden in the game and you will need to use external tools to figure out the number if you want to min max it.

&nbsp;

**\*\*August 2026 update JP version only | 5.5 Anniversary update**

A new QOL has been added to the JP version. Compatibility numbers are now displayed and individual breakdowns can be shown. I'm not going to retroactively tweak the rest of my guide to accommodate this visibility update, so all you get will be this note.

While the game displays a single cumulative symbol (◎/〇/△), the underlying math is actually the sum of several **Individual Compatibility** links.

**Individual Compatibility** is the hidden point value assigned to a specific parent or grandparent in your lineage. The "Overall" symbol is simply the final result of these separate individual links being added together. This will be visited in greater detail in later chapters.

**Why it matters**: You might see a ◎  "Overall" rating and think the parents are a perfect match,but it may just be the sum of poor compatibilities, ie 50 \+25 \+25 \+ 50 \+ 25 \+ 25 \= 150\. You should definitely worry if you do not see ◎ before starting a run.&nbsp;&nbsp;

Ideally you’d want your overall compatibility above 300, optimally around 500\.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**There is no bonus compatibility from running any same race a second time.** For example, winning Arima Kinen in Classic or Senior contributes the same compatibility as winning it once.

&nbsp;

**PS:** The effects of compatibility and inheritance genes stop at the grandparent level. There is no hidden mechanic for having a parent Uma Musume with 100 generations behind her.

# **How can you control these points?**

\*24 June 2026\. Global is now using the updated compatibility system.

**The Current System (JP Post-2.0 anniversary / Grand Masters and beyond scenarios)**

> The compatibility system has been revamped to only count racing G1 races.

> * **G1 Only:** Only overlapping G1 races now grant bonus compatibility.  
> * **Simplified Gains:** G2/G3 races and Title bonuses (Triple Crown/Tiara) **no longer contribute.**  
> * **Increased Value:** G1 races now grant **\+3 points each** (previously \+1), and the base compatibility for Umas has been boosted across the board.  
> * **Parent to Parent** overlapping races now count towards compatibility.

### **General Parenting Strategy**

You should always run the maximum number of G1s available to you, as achieving ◎ compatibility is now significantly more straightforward than before. This also means that you should modify your aptitudes to be able to race in mile and dirt races if possible.

&nbsp;

As a rule of thumb, overlap as many **G1s** as possible for a respectable compatibility bonus. The ideal race count is between 22 to 26 when including dirt rotations. With enough overlapping races, it is entirely possible to achieve ◎ compatibility using only **one side** of the parentage line. Sample Urara below with ◎ from just ONE side.

![][image5]

## **Recommendations:**&nbsp;

Ever since the 2.0 anniversary compatibility overhaul, I think it is overkill to place too much emphasis on Uma to Uma compatibility. Bonus races already account for the bulk of your compatibility.

Just race every G1 race, 20\~ if you do turf only, 26+ with dirt. Take care about mixing Tiara and Crown race rotation Umas as this means less races overlap and reduces compatibility from the ideal max.&nbsp;

The ideal way to bridge the compatibility loss with Tiara vs Triple Crown rotations is by enabling dirt racing via raising dirt aptitudes, or alternatively on modern scenarios that do not have objective races.

##  **Global Section (URA to GL scenario) \- Legacy Compatibility**

**\*\* This legacy compatibility system is currently obsolete for all different server region versions of the game as of 24 June 2026**  
Apparently Cygames (Global) decided to push the compatibility system earlier and it is no longer delayed till the 2.0 Anniversary patch (GM scenario)

**⚠️**The Global server currently uses the "Legacy" compatibility system. However, once the 2.0 anniversary update arrives, G2 and G3 races will stop providing compatibility bonuses. The compatibility for parents created using mainly G2/G3 races will significantly drop in the future.&nbsp;

**Take note**: Because the current system counts G1, G2, and G3 races, you can currently build "Super Parents" with insane compatibility scores, **preferably** while in **MANT scenario**, by stacking everyone in your lineage with 60+ overlapping wins.&nbsp;

### **Raising Compatibility**

In the legacy compatibility system, bonus compatibility is created via stacking overlapping races across your parenting lineage with bonuses from assembling titles/epithets.

* **Races:** For every identical race win (**G1, G2, or G3**) shared between a parent/grandparent and the target horse, you gain **\+1 compatibility point**.  
* **Title Bonuses:** Obtaining specific title/epithets (e.g., Triple Crown or Triple Tiara) grants an additional **\+1 point per title.**  
* **Individual Links:** These points are calculated individually for every connection in your family tree (Left side vs. Right side).

\*Reminder that there is no bonus compatibility from running any same race a second time.

It is entirely possible that you may build super parents by running and winning the same 63 races for both parents A & B for a bonus of over 150 points to compatibility.

# **Calculating Compatibility**

&nbsp;

Back to compatibility calculations.

&nbsp;

Screenshotted below is a reference from derpiederp’s sheet for better visualisation of how compatibility is calculated.

The individual compatibility of each Parent/ GP is calculated based on their compatibility with the other respective Uma (P1-\>gp1) \+ respective bonuses, visualised by the \+ in between each relevant link.

![][image8]

(I’ve been told that the parent to parent race compatibility in the screenshot shouldn’t exist in the legacy compatibility yet and has been removed in his calculator, so this screenshot might be outdated)&nbsp;

&nbsp;

As you can see each side of the Individual compatibility on the parent side has 3 bonus relationships that depend on the race and uma to uma compatibility, hence maxing out your races has much more weightage on compatibility than the uma to uma bonuses.

My take on compatibility values is: You don’t need to know how to calculate any of this unless you **really really NEED** to feed the knowledge for hunger of the exact numbers that go into calculating your odds of inheriting the different genes.

# **自主トレ育成 / Background auto / Independant training**&nbsp;

Cygames has introduced background auto to JP servers on 30 June 2026 and announced that its coming to Global servers too in early July 2026\.

&nbsp;

Screenshots will be from the JP version unless someone who plays global wants to feed me the relevant screenshots.

&nbsp;

I originally thought a guide wasn't necessary for background auto since it's so straightforward, but I realised people kept asking the same questions or just didn't understand how it works so… Here I am.

&nbsp;

**What is this new function?**

Background auto is a new function that allows you to schedule an automated run in the background. This is an updated QOL for the auto-kun function released for JP server but it is a completely fresh new feature for Global server.

&nbsp;

What this does is it runs auto training in the background over a fixed time of 50 minutes per run. Unlike auto-kun who can be summoned to take the wheel in certain scenarios, you are allowed to use background auto in EVERY scenario without restrictions.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**What are the pros and cons of using normal auto-kun or Background auto?**

Both of them are assumed to use the same auto-logic and will suck for certain scenarios with heavy mechanics.

&nbsp;

Auto-kun:&nbsp;

Pros&nbsp;

- Faster than BG auto, as fast as 15mins for URA, 25-35 mins on ramen scenario.  
- You can win races at better odds especially when parent farming with large consecutive race stretches.&nbsp;

Cons

- Requires your device to be active for the duration of the run.&nbsp;  
- Requires manual intervention if you enabled certain options such as manual inheritance picking (Umaplan users only) or pause during x event.

&nbsp;

Background auto:&nbsp;

Pros

- Can be done in the background and you can actually watch the Uma Musume bond stories, live theatre and other game events you normally wouldn’t be able to do while playing.  
- Can never fail the run, all objective races are automatically won.  
- Guaranteed wins against difficult opponents during objective races, but has a dual-edged edge problem, elaborated below..

Cons

- Winning races is chance-based. Your aptitude (ranked A to G) affects win probability — higher is better. However, certain Umas can still win races reliably even with low (C or D) aptitudes. Since background auto tends to pick up random race losses, using auto-kun may give much better overall compatibility  
- All runs are fixed at 50 minutes and cannot be interrupted nor influenced. If you somehow decide u want to play the game manually, you cant intervene and will need to wait or delete the run.

&nbsp;

**Special race win chance mechanics**

Races in this mode use a completely different mechanic to determine if you win the race or not.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

1. You can bypass races with overpowered opponents via rolling the race winning odds. For example \- Umas like Narita Brian, Sakura Laurel, Verxina, or Curren Bouquet’dor who normally face Gorilla’s, bears or extinction tier threats during their respective races will have no problem can still come in 1st as they will be rolling a 110% chance to win these races.  
2. Objective races \- You will only auto win all objective races that **if failed**, will end the run. For example, this doesn’t mean u’ll win Urara’s objective race for Arima Kinen, if you have her default aptitudes \- as this objective does not fail her run.  
3. Non objective races

Your stats will not be factored into the odds of winning races. Instead, the win chances of entering races are purely percentage-based, following the same odds as the Green Ticket/Inheritance-only Umas. If you are interested to learn more about this system, it has its own section later in the guide found [here](#inheritance-only-uma-musume-/-継承専用ウマ娘).&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Your odds of winning a race begins at 110% if you have A/A distance and ground aptitude for the corresponding race you are entering. (**Cygames provided this number**)

S aptitude has been known to function the same as A aptitude, also beginning at 110%

&nbsp;

The odds will be lowered for each aptitude below A, and will drop even further for every consecutive race you run starting from the 4th turn. Cygames did not provide any details on the exact odds it will be lowered by. However, our trusty lad Shoppo\_ura has spent the time investigating the odds.

&nbsp;

Shoppo’s tweet here [https://x.com/shoppo\_ura/status/2071769445605999036?s=20](https://x.com/shoppo_ura/status/2071769445605999036?s=20) with his table of results.

&nbsp;

If you look closely at the data, the win rate is actually completely unaffected at less than 3 (\<3) and at exactly 3\. For example, at A/A aptitude, both "\<3" and "3" consecutive races maintain a perfect 100% win rate. The penalty only starts dropping the odds once you hit 4 or more consecutive races.

&nbsp;

Shoppo also investigated win rate reduction for running consecutive races @&nbsp;  
[https://x.com/shoppo\_ura/status/2077988949495279684?s=20](https://x.com/shoppo_ura/status/2077988949495279684?s=20)&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Essentially aptitudes for ground and distance have the same weightage. Meaning AG \= GA \= DD

**Deeper explanations for setting it up**

![][image10]

Left: Original screenshot

Right: AI generated (gemini) translated version

&nbsp;

This screen is located just before you begin your run and you can select between normal training or background auto.

&nbsp;

If you expand on the deck details it will just show you your selected uma and the parents/deck you had set up before coming to this screen, sample on the right.

&nbsp;

For the first set of options, you’ll need to specify which kind of stats to focus on.

Balanced \= balanced stat distribution, Stamina \- higher stamina focus, Sprint \- no stamina focus.

&nbsp;

Next is **Skill Hint Prioritization**.

*Note: BG Auto will NOT buy skills during your run.*

These settings simply force Auto-kun to:

1. Click on support cards with an active **"\!"** hint event if they offer these specific skills.  
2. Pick event choices that grant the corresponding skill.

\*While Cygames hasn’t explicitly explained how background runs are simulated, post-run data suggests they follow the same decision-making system as Auto-kun.

&nbsp;

In my screenshot above you can see that I’ve placed straight line recovery in the hint priority list. I recommend always including Straight Line Recovery to your hint priority list. By default, Auto-kun gambles on the top option for the random Anshinzawa event, which has a massive 80% failure rate and devastating penalties (-2 mood, lost stats, or Insomnia)

&nbsp;

Doing this forces Auto-kun to pick her second option instead. This safer route rewards Corner/Straight Recovery and has a much better 50% success rate, drastically reducing the penalties if it fails.&nbsp;

Ideally if you don’t wish to gamble on 50% odds, the better choice would be the 3rd or 4th option for Anshinzawa’s event. However this cannot be conveyed to auto-kun as no skills are attached to these options.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

# **Scenario Parent Farming Recommendations**

Here I’ll rate individual scenarios for parent runs.&nbsp;

- I’ll use stars to rate each scenario for parent farming.&nbsp;  
- **The maximum stars is 5**  
- Scenarios will be rated on how easy it is to raise stats, ease of gameplay mechanics and amount of SP you can gain.&nbsp;

You can jump to the TL;DR section for a quick final summary of the scenarios.

&nbsp;

**Preface**: Ever since auto has been added to the game, all scenario guides will be written in mind that auto-kun will be controlling the wheel. Guides will only be focused on parenting and Ace runs should not be following my guides.

###  **URA \[Auto enabled 2025\]**

Post 2.0 remake, you can get nice unique scenario genes but it is still difficult to consistently roll SS grade or above Umas.  
With the 4th Anniversary update, this scenario now has the **auto-run** function.

&nbsp;

Auto time: 15-20 minutes

Manual time: 20-30 minutes

Launch of Scenario: Expect 1k+ skill points

Post **rework**: Expect around 2k Skill points&nbsp;

Rating **(After rework): ☆** \- only if you want the new scenario skill genes.&nbsp;

Essence skiills are great to inherit especially レースの真髄・体  is a top tier gene for every uma&nbsp;

### **Aoharu / Unity Cup**

\- Fast with huge race RNG but you won’t be consistently rolling SS grade or above Umas.&nbsp;

Max is S+ rank with mega whale cards./ SS only possible post rework.

&nbsp;

Launch: Expect around 1-1.5k Skill points  
Post rework: Expect 2k Skill points or less

Launch of Scenario: **☆☆☆**&nbsp;

Rating (**After rework but before GM): ☆☆**

&nbsp;

**Why choose Aoharu over URA?**

You get more random hints from bursting the gauges. Your average stat lines are higher than URA, having Riko in your deck gives \~ 150 Stamina/100 Guts for free from her dates, events and end of run bonuses. You hit the rest button way less than URA if you play it right, bring INT cards / burst on Int for energy. Base energy consumption is lower too.&nbsp;

### **Make a New Track**

Runs here take close to over an hour to do, 45 minutes if you are a god. Run times are cut by 33% faster after the event speed up QOL is implemented. Originally this QOL was added together with GL’s launch but Global may get it earlier. I don’t work for cygames so I dont know what they would do.

Take note that the G2/G3 races will be useless for compatibility after the compatibility rework.  
This is a “racist” scenario \- If the uma cannot run **mile** races, they cannot play this scenario well. Rip Tamamo and Eishin flash (released just before this scenario)

Launch of Scenario: **☆☆☆☆☆ The perfect scenario for farming the next half of the year.**&nbsp;

* **Compatibility:** It is incredibly easy to stack **50–63 bonus race points** for all Umas, provided they can run mile/mid races.  
* **Stats & Factors:** You gain significant "free" stats just by progressing the run. Furthermore, the scenario’s **Climax genes** give Stamina and Guts—the best possible combination. (I personally favour Stamina as a bonus stat, you will find out why when GL comes)  
* **Longevity:**  This is a **God-tier scenario** for parenting, though the honeymoon period will not last forever. While it currently provides "mega" compatibility, it will eventually be phased out with the compatibility overhaul when GM arrives

Expected SP: Around 2k\~ 2.5k  Depends on deck but there's not a lot of variance.

&nbsp;

Current Rating: **Obsolete**

### **LARC**

\- LARC is fast and pretty easy. It introduces new **Mini-scenario Genes** in addition to the main **Scenario Gene**, both of which provide individual stat bonuses. Bonus: This is a shortened scenario so you can complete runs in as fast as 15 minutes.

&nbsp;

Launch of Scenario: **☆☆☆☆,** not 5 because max compatibility is MUCH lower compared to any other scenario.

Current Rating**: ☆☆ (pre 2026\) / Superseded & obsolete**&nbsp;

I’m recommending this scenario **ONLY** to bridge the compatibility gap for Umas with extremely limited aptitudes such as Short only, mile only, dirt only, see notes below.

Expect about 2.5-3.5k SP depending on deck & luck, this scenario is **not** suited for weak parent decks. Bring at least 2 speed cards \+ Mei’s friend card or you WILL lose the scenario races\!

\*Special LARC Notes: Keep in mind that L'Arc modifies the aptitudes of all Umas to **A-rank for Turf and Mid-distance**. This allows you to bridge compatibility between Umas who usually have incompatible ranges—such as pairing a Turf,Short-distance specialist like **Curren Chan** with Mid-distance parents like **Narita Brian**. This also applies to bridging Umas who only have Dirt aptitudes.

However, if you want to roll for **Turf or Mid-distance Factors** at the end of the run, you must still naturally raise those aptitudes to **A-rank**. The scenario buff is temporary and does not make these Turf or Mid red genes eligible for gene generation.

**Mini Scenario Whites:** In order for the new scenario whites to have a chance to appear, you will need to have maxed out the relevant debuff level ups during the run.

&nbsp;

**However**, this shortened scenario limits the total races you can do as compared to a regular length scenario. Your compatibility will be significantly limited here compared to the others.

&nbsp;

If you want to farm for parents here I would recommend you train your parent lineages from the same scenario, ie. Using LARC’s grandparents to train your LARC parents to overlap the same LARC race rotations, but you will need to defeat Venus & Montjeu in their respective races to unlock the LARC debuff\! Remember to buy skills.

# **2024’s Scenarios Foreword:**&nbsp;

**2024 Scenarios (UAF / GFF / Mecha)** The three scenarios launched in 2024 significantly changed the inheritance meta. Unlike previous scenarios, this set **does not generate "Big" Scenario Genes** (which traditionally grant up to \+30/+30 stats). Instead, they produce scenario-specific genes:

* **UAF:** Generates 3 unique genes with a mix of stats.  
* **GFF & Mecha:** Generate 5 unique genes (one for each individual stat).  
* These Mini scenario genes are the only genes that can directly give Skill points.  
  &nbsp;

If you inherit at least 3 of the corresponding scenario’s genes mid run, they will grant you a new unique skill, unique to each scenario. PS: These skills are underwhelming and not worth the effort of target-farming the genes. Crucially, these special skills **cannot be passed down as genes** themselves.

&nbsp;

Cygames has also changed the scenario launch schedule here, future scenarios now will come out every 4 months instead of 6\.&nbsp;

### 

### **UAF**&nbsp;

Initially better than LARC, but the GFF and Mecha scenarios immediately superseded this scenario.

Launch of Scenario: **☆☆☆☆**&nbsp;

Rating (2025): **Superseded & obsolete**

&nbsp;

**\*\*This Scenario does not have a main Gene. The possible genes are split across 3 unique stat specific mini genes that grants you a unique skill mid run if you proc at least 3 of them across both inheritances. Sadly, the skill isn't worth taking.**

### **Grand Food Festival / Farming scenario**

Expect to get up to 4.0 to 5k skill points when running this scenario depending on the deck used.&nbsp;  
**Advanced Strategy: Hint Pool Manipulation** If you "prune" your skills by exhausting the available skill hint list early in a run, you can force the game to provide random hints from outside your current deck. The new hints that appear are determined by your Uma’s **A-rank aptitudes** (Distance, Surface, and Strategy).

Average runs in GFF take 45 minutes to 1 hour, longer if your device takes longer to load new scenes/menus.  
Mandatory card: Director Akikawa Yayoi

Initial rating: **☆☆☆☆**

Current Rating: **Superseded & obsolete**&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**\*\*This Scenario does not have a main Gene. The possible genes are split across 5 unique stat specific mini genes that grants you a unique skill mid run if you proc at least 3 of them across both inheritances. Sadly, the skill isn't worth taking.**

### **Mecha Scenario**

Expect almost equal or slighter lesser SP as compared to GFF but this scenario is MUCH faster as there are less scenario specific menu items to click through.  
Note: You are unable to generate extra skills outside of your deck in this scenario. Do GFF instead if you want that.

Average time: 30 to 45 minutes

Mandatory card: Scenario \[Stamina card: Air shakur\] or any Biwa hayahide card  
Initial rating: **☆☆☆☆**&nbsp;  
Current Rating: **Superseded & obsolete**

&nbsp;

**\*\*This Scenario does not have a main Gene. The possible genes are split across 5 unique stat specific mini genes that grants you a unique skill mid run if you proc at least 3 of them across both inheritances. Sadly, the skill isn't worth taking.**

# **Feb 2025, Auto-run function released**

Starting from  all future scenarios listed below, Auto-runs are enabled and parenting isn’t a chore anymore\!&nbsp;  
It's actually normal to run out of 10 or 15 rentals depending if the ½ tp campaign is running.  The downside of auto is, if you happen to be a mobile-only player, you can’t use your phone while auto-running, unless you are a fold screen phone user with adhd.

&nbsp;

You can also turn on auto clocking for failed races. Take note that the June 2025 update gives you the option to turn off clocking for bad aptitude races. Ie dober running for Arima Kinen will no longer kill your clocks. What's determined as bad aptitude is C and below. However, C still has a very good chance of winning so turning this on may possibly lead to wasted races that could have been won.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Early DYI VS Onsen scenario comparisons:**

~~I’m not sure if I'm doing it wrong but I don't see how this scenario is good for parenting. This could be my first recommendation to avoid a new scenario for parenting runs.~~&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Eyeballing the results from auto-running both scenarios, targeting a minimum of **UE** rank, both DYI and Onsen scenarios yield comparable results when running approximately 28 races, (only G1s, with no secret genes chasing.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

This performance parity quickly disappears as the race count increases: Onsen scenario will start to fall behind DYI on SP/hints. Above 30 races, the runs will completely start to break down due to slower digging speeds. While Onsen potentially can generate more Skill Points, it suffers from a significantly lower rate of hint generation from random \! hints and hints from super onsen procs. Don’t count on auto-kun to effectively utilise Onsen's mechanics, especially Onsen activations.

&nbsp;

For your auto runs to effectively generate 6k and above SP, you will need to complete the 2 Onsens that generate extra support on onsen ticket uses. Ie, Yukoma Onsen before Senior summer, AND Legendary Onsen before URA finals (preferably 4 turns after it first appears).

If your deck contains more than 3 0LB-2LB stuff, runs on DYI *may* fare better, go test it.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Auto Run Setup**

The setup on the right is the JP community’s agreed upon most optimal priority list. If your run does not complete the legendary onsen, it's going to suffer for hints. You can swap the int/event one from 5 \- \> 4 for \+20-30 SP on debut race but auto-kun doesn't always proc the onsen ticket on races  when required.

&nbsp;

**Deck choice**: Extremely inflexible \- you require 5 different card types for scenario mechanic bonuses for 3 of your supports to appear in training after digging the ![][image16]onsen. This mechanic is similar to Mecha scenario’s and probably not so relevant if you are racing hard in senior year.

&nbsp;

**Note**: It doesn't matter whether you use SSR or R Kiyoko here \- since Auto-kun doesn't use the onsen mechanics effectively in the first place.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Mid-November 2025** update: Actually \>30 races can also be done, but they need to be strategically planned. Racing works well on parts of the run where the onsen digging speed doesn't matter. Examples; The entirety of Junior year, since you only need 2 onsens there to advance the onsen level. Or inserting a race into an onsen dig that does not make you finish it slower. However this is mainly geared towards G2/G3 races that don’t add to compatibility, but may trigger some hidden genes.

&nbsp;

**This Scenario does not have any extra scenario specific gene.**

&nbsp;

**Compatibility considerations: Good 4/5**&nbsp;

There can be **race mismatches** due to differing objective races depending on which end race you pick. So **make sure** you plan your parents with the **same** end objective race.

A benefit from this scenario: Tiara route Umas can now be forced onto triple Crown routes. The ideal path would be aligning them all to **either** BC Turf’s route (Runs Nippon derby, Japan Cup and Takarazuka Kinen) **Or** BC Filly & Mare Turf where you can fit in Tiara AND more total races.

&nbsp;

Under any breeders cup route, while you do lose 2-3 standard G1 races worth of compatibility when paired with other scenarios, you do have an additional 1 G1 gain from the Breeder cup objective race when pairing parents who have also been trained under BC scenario.&nbsp;

That's a lot of turns lost to heal and fix mood. Sample RIP training turn below

The scenario’s hint mechanic is similar to Mecha Scenario where you can obtain ALL hints that are present in the same training facility once you reach technique level 5\. This is only available in the later half of the classic year.  **However**, it is severely hampered by the sheer amount of races you need to do in parenting runs.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Note that you can also get free hints at each scenario checkpoint\! Just extrapolating here, if you max out all your hints early you could even get hints outside of your deck if all obtainable skills are exhausted. However, this seems highly impossible without heavy pruning due to your inability to generate enough hints by senior year unless your decks are majorly scuffed. Example: Your total skill count in the deck is less than 30, aka. your deck mainly consists of Year 1 release cards and we shouldn't even be parenting here.

&nbsp;

**Stat gains: Ok 3/5**

Main stat gains are high while off stats gains are really low, if you do not bring a certain card type, that stat will suffer. The highs are high and the lows are really low. **Stamina,** I’m looking at you.

# **Stat Uncap Mechanics**

(**For Global players**: This section does not apply to you until the stat cap is raised beyond 1200\)

Stat Uncap refers to the increase in maximum stat limits gained by inheriting certain genes.

Stat uncaps are affected by the quality of your blue genes during both the initial and mid-run inheritance stages. In the middle of a run, inheriting a green gene also increases the stat cap based on bonuses from the source Uma Musume. For example, Seiun's "Angling" uncaps Stamina and Intelligence following her Uma’s bonus in Stamina & Int , while Kitasan Black's "Wasshoi" uncaps Speed and Stamina. The precise amount of the stat uncap is currently unknown, but not a significant number (usually single digits).

&nbsp;

**Update**: You can view which stat will be increased by clicking on their Green Genes. Agnes digital’s unique raises speed/stam/power (int is not raised even though she also has bonus there)

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

| **White Gene (Skills) (1 hint per ☆)** | 1 to 5 hint bonus Minimum of \+1 hint | ?? rangeMinimum of \+1 hint | ?? range Minimum of \+1 hint |
| **Green gene (Unique skills) (1 hint per ☆)** | 1 to 5 hint bonus Minimum of \+1 hint | ?? range Minimum of \+1 hint | Negative hints at beginning of run, ie 3 ☆ Gene but only get \+1 hint |
| **Red gene** | 1-5 points^ | 1-5 points^ | 1-5 points^ |

Take note that even though this isn't applied before the run starts, the roll is not RNG and the hint grade obtained will always be the same for any run. Ie. you will see the same lowered green hint level for △ compatibilities.

Red: No limit

# **Good/Poor Compatibility**

~~I don't have data and do not want to investigate the data for poor compatibility, there is no merit to running △ parents at all,~~ 〇 compatibility should be the lowest you are willing to go for Champion Meeting whacky builds.

&nbsp;

What do you mean by whacky build?&nbsp;  
A prime example of a "whacky build" is trying to re-engineer Halloween Super Creek to be able to run for short distance races. This was a popular (but highly unsuccessful) strategy to allow her to run as an ace for a Short CM, or to generate Short Red genes. However raising the Short Distance aptitude to A or S rank, despite her initial G rating is extremely challenging. Players did this as her unique skill is highly effective in short races. Which surfaces a new problem, as goal typically necessitates using **parents of lower compatibility**, such as △ or 〇. The cause of this is that Umas who naturally have a **chance to pass on short aptitude** follow different race rotations and also have poor base compatibility with her. As you can see, raising G aptitude is a tough wall to climb, especially for Halloween Super Creek.

## **Individual compatibility theory**

There's some ~~minor empirical~~ concrete evidence that the individual compatibility is how it works instead of the overall compatibility theory. \- **View bonus chapter below for the full breakdown.**

&nbsp;

Hidden compatibility example:

    Parent 1 : ◎				Parent 2: ◯

/                \\                                	 /		 \\

Gp1.1 ◯	GP1.2 △		GP2.1:◯		Gp2.2: ◯

&nbsp;

Even if your initial compatibility rating is excellent (◎), you might encounter significantly lower-than-expected gene proc rates due to poor gene inheritance from Grandparent 1.2 and a reduced proc chance in the entire Parent 2 lineage.&nbsp;

This means that despite a seemingly perfect starting point ◎, the actual outcome of the gene inheritance turn could be negatively impacted by the hidden compatibility factors.

&nbsp;

Example 1:  
Base compatibility numbers are displayed, without overlapping races bonuses.![][image52]  
Fuji Kiseki is the weakest link here as she has poor base compatibility with Kitasan (and most other Mid/long Umas). So her genes would likely have the lowest proc rate among the entire lineage if the overlapping races are low.&nbsp;

Fuji Kiseki also has E aptitude in long distances as compared to the rest in this family tree, and also different mandatory objective races.. This means a mismatch of at least 3 races of compatibility, Kikkasho \+ Arima \+ Haruten, if you do not adjust for long distance (which is a new hassle on its own too)

&nbsp;

Personal Example 2 (no maths data)

&nbsp;

![][image53]

&nbsp;

**Fuji Kiseki’s genes (shortened)**

![][image54]

An example of this was observed when playing approximately 20 runs with the above setup.&nbsp;

Fuji Kiseki had a 3 star green gene which means inheriting her unique skill should provide \+3 hints more often than not. However I realised she tended to give me \+1-2 hints whenever her green inheritance proc-ed during the 20 ish runs.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Disclaimer: This particular example is empirical evidence so don't read too much into it. Not a concern if you are maxing out compatibility as you should be in the first place.

## **Gene proc rates (without compatibility)**

Proc rates are determined by the ★ of the gene & compatibility (◎ \> 〇 \> △) .

3★ genes have higher proc rates and should give better quality (hint levels) than 1★ or 2★ genes&nbsp;

**Misinformation update**: I don’t know why people are saying nonsense like each gene can only proc once in the entire run. You **CAN** see the same gene proc again in the second inheritance event..

For those wondering why my guide doesn’t go in depth into the exact proc rates\*, remember that my guide primarily focuses on gene generation. It's important to note that data collection on gene proc rates is often muddled and subject to bias. This stems from concerns regarding data collection reliability and the sheer number of variables involved, compounded by the hidden compatibility numbers, which makes accurate data collection particularly challenging to verify.&nbsp;

Furthermore, readers should be wary of guides from **certain** individuals who lack a deep understanding of the game, yet present **obscure information** as definitive insights.  
**Lastly and most importantly**, it shouldn’t matter what the proc rate is because you cannot influence it beyond just going for max compatibility, which should **already** be done.

**Extreme factor modification example**&nbsp;

Where you are trying to raise your uma’s aptitude from G to A/S.&nbsp;

Using Agnes Digital below as an example for raising G \-\> S for long distance.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

For the best odds:

1: You will need at least 10\* Red genes in long to push her initial inheritance from G to C at the start of the run.

In another case, you may also raise C-\>B on the first inheritance with at least 1 proc, and then during the second inheritance, you’d only need 1 point for B-\>A or at least 4points for B \-\> S.

# **What do Red Genes do and why do you want them?**

Red genes will raise the aptitude of your Uma in the following respective areas

Ground: Turf or Dirt

Distance: Short, Mile , Mid , Long&nbsp;

Strategy:	Nige , Senkou , Sashi , Oiko&nbsp;

Runner , Leader , Betweener , Chaser

&nbsp;

Your stats are affected by the aptitude that your uma has.

Look below for the table of how each aptitude affects the stats&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Data sourced from early 2021:

&nbsp;

| Aptitudes | G | F | E | D | C | B | A | S |
| :---- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Ground**&nbsp; | 10.00% | 30.00% | 50.00% | 70.00% | 80.00% | 90.00% | 100.00% | **105.00%** |
| **Distance** | 10.00% | 20.00% | 40.00% | 60.00% | 80.00% | 90.00% | 100.00% | **105.00%** |
| **Strategy**&nbsp; | 10.00% | 20.00% | 40.00% | 60.00% | 75.00% | 85.00% | 100.00% | **110.00%** |

At aptitudes E and below you also get negative Acceleration debuffs.&nbsp;

While most people prioritise getting S-rank distance aptitudes, a lesser-known fact is that an **S-rank strategy aptitude provides** more benefits for Runners (*Nige*) than for other styles. This is primarily due to how the INT stat governs the "Position Keep" and "Fight for the Lead" mechanics.

The Fight for lead mechanic was only added after 2.0 anniversary? Don’t remember the exact date. Nige umas consume more stamina at the opening leg \- also dependent on guts to fight for the lead.

Meanwhile, Oonige just puts speed & stam consumption into overdrive as compared to Nige counterparts.

&nbsp;

**Feb 2026,** As an added bonus to aiming for S-ranked strategy, there is now an overINT mechanic where having INT over will increase the skill power to Unique/Gold/Pink skills, inherited ults are not counted.&nbsp;

# **Hidden Red Gene values:**

**Original research**, I’ve chanced upon this on 25th January 2022 while attempting to do some 魔改造 (Extreme modification) for the Short Champions meeting at that time.

***\*\***This really only matters when trying to raise extreme aptitudes beginning from G and F.*&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Red genes have been discovered to also follow some hidden value proc. For easier visualisation, **my theory** is that it follows the same \+1 to \+5 value mechanics as the Green/white genes. This means that you may end up rolling the lower end of \+1 value even if you proc a 3☆ Red Gene.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Example 1 **High Roll** : Starting at G \> C initially with cumulative 10☆ Red genes on your lineage. During inheritance, it is possible to reach A from C with ONE inheritance of the Red gene if you roll a hidden \+4 or 5 value. Since C \> A requires at least 4 red gene points&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Example 2 **High roll** : Starting at F \> B initially with cumulative 10☆ Red genes on your lineage. This could also allow you to hit S aptitude with only ONE red gene proc Since B \> A \> S could happen if you roll 4 points and above.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Example 3 **Low roll/Standard roll** : G \> C initially It is possible that you only reach B aptitude even if two red 3\* inheritances were rolled on the same inherit turn.&nbsp;  
![][image56]&nbsp;

This is what it looks like **(mid run inherits only)**

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Unfortunately as the red gene value is hidden, all of this data is from inference rather than actual empirical data and I do not have any statistics.**

# **Chapter 4: Gene generation mechanics & farming strategies for the different grades of genes**

# **Red Genes ( Strategy, Ground ability, Distance)**

&nbsp;

The red gene can only be randomly generated from aptitudes the Uma Musume has scored A in; Dirt/turf, distance and strategy.

So if you wish to target certain red genes, you will need to raise the target aptitude to an A grade or above while **not** raising any unwanted aptitude to A.

&nbsp;

Example 1: Mayano Topgun has B grade running strategies in Sashi/Betweener & Oikomi/Chaser, these last 2 aptitudes will never be picked for inheritance unless you raise it to A grade.

&nbsp;

Example 2: El condor pasa has B grade in Dirt tracks, and will not generate the Dirt gene unless it has been boosted to A or above.

&nbsp;

Fun facts: At the initial launch of the game, the only way to initially obtain dirt genes was to roll a dirt gene on Haru Urara since she was the only Umnya to have dirt at A and then use her to pass the dirt gene down to another parent.

# **Example of a failed/bad red inheritance** {#example-of-a-failed/bad-red-inheritance}

&nbsp;

Using Symboli Rudolph as an example, she is generally sought after as a strong ~~stallion for breeding~~ parent for 先行/差し/追込 Leader/betweener/chaser mainly because of her unique skill.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Her unique skill activates if she overtakes 3 other horses during the last leg.

However, her unique skill will be useless when paired with Runner / 逃げ horses since they won't be doing any overtaking. Therefore, you would normally not want her to inherit nor pass down the Runner red gene since it is basically useless for her offspring.

But mistakes can happen..&nbsp;

**![][image57]**

&nbsp;

**So how did this happen?**

Symboli Rudolph’s base Runner / 逃げ aptitude is B so it would normally not be generated.

My Mayano had a red Nige gene, causing Rudolf's 逃げ aptitude to grow from B \-\> A & therefore made Rudolph eligible for the gene generation.

This happened during the early stages of my account as Mayano was my second 3☆, so I used her in the hopes of making my first 9☆. I succeeded in creating my first 9☆ but ended up with undesirable red genes.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**What should you actually do?**

Given the luxury of choice, do not pair your target girl with parents that may lead to a generation of conflicting strategies. Do not get tricked into pairing conflicting strategies into parenting lineages even if they have the matching red gene ie. 6 Mid gene but unusable white genes.

Bad Example 2\. Producing Goldship with Senkou as her red gene because her aptitude was raised to A (unless that's what you want for whatever weird reason)

![][image58]

Why is 先行/Leader bad for her in this specific example? Because Goldship's unique skill only activates when she is in the back, later 50% of the race, a good chance that this only occurs if you run sashi/oiko 差し/追込.

Secondly, the skills available to her are all backrow or Oiko focused. Even if you have many whites, most of them will be useless and unusable when you try to use her for senkou parenting.

&nbsp;

**The ideal parent strategy**&nbsp;

Try to pair Uma museums with similar running style and distance together so that there are more common genes in the lineage. This allows you to&nbsp;

1. Have a higher chance of producing a large white pool due to increased generation chances.&nbsp;  
2. Have usable inherited ults when using the parent

Runner/Nige Example.  
**![][image59]**

Kitasan is being paired with two other runners with useful and overlapping skill genes for bonus gene generation & inheritance chances.

# **Generating Blue Genes**&nbsp;

&nbsp;

At the end of each run, 1 stat will be picked among your 5 stats and a roll will be done to determine what ★ you receive.

This means that you will have a 1 in 5 or 20% chance of rolling for any individual stat as your generated blue gene.

&nbsp;

Next, the game checks under which grade your selected stat is and a 2nd roll is conducted according to the chart below.

In order to be able to be eligible to obtain a 3★ blue gene, the selected status must be at least B rank or higher, above 600 stats.

&nbsp;

| 1150\~1200 (SS+) | 254 | 820 | 128 | 10.65% |
| 1100\~1149 (SS) | 218 | 740 | 118 | 10.97% |

**Methods of farming for 3★ blue stats**

By combining all of the the theories above, your adjusted odds of receiving a 3★ are listed in the chart below.![][image60]

For example, ending your run with the stats listed below will mean you have approximately overall 3% chance of obtaining a 3★ blue stat in either speed or power.

![][image61]

1 SS stat \+ 1 B stat

(10% \* 20%) \+ (5% \* 20%) \= (speed)**2%** \+ (power)**1%** \= **3%**

&nbsp;

When I first created this guide, Aoharu scenario was the newest scenario. It was previously impossible to get SS in all 5 stats for the maximum chance of 10%, and the average person's odds were around 3-6%.

However with the introduction of the Grand Masters & LARC scenarios and later scenarios, an all SS statline is actually possible now, elaborated more at the end of this chapter.

&nbsp;

**Basic information about skill genes:**

&nbsp;

You can only generate a skill gene if you learnt the skill during the run. Even if all 6 of your parents/grandparents have the skill, but you did not pick the skill, it will **not** be generated / passed down.

&nbsp;

You may only generate the basic version of any skill, no Gold version can ever be passed down. However, it is still advisable to buy gold skills if you really want to pass down that specific skill, the why will be explained further below.

&nbsp;

Take note that unique skills (green) that have been inherited cannot be passed down as a white gene. Unless you are buying it for a very specific reason, to help win races mid run, it ultimately is a waste of skill points during a parent farm run.

**Special note:** If you inherit a skill which you have already learnt during an inheritance event, that skill's hint will be converted into stats.

I have no data as to which stat and what amount will be given in place of the hint but from experience it is usually a small value between 1-9.

&nbsp;

**Example situation:** You have already learnt 良バ場 ○ and receive an inheritance for 良バ場. Even though you can still learn 良バ場◎, you will be given stats instead of additional hint discounts since it’s treated as a skill that you’ve already bought.

However do take note of another aspect of skill hint mechanics:  
Example 2: You have already learnt 良バ場 ○, **\!** skill hints or end of race hints will never proc this skill for additional hints. The only way to gain additional hints for it now is to trigger the hint from a unique event with choices or a card event.

Learning the gold version of a skill will increase the odds of your gene generation to a minimum of 40% and maximum of 70%

Learning ◎ of said skill gives better chances for a min/max of 25%/30% from this data set and so on. By extrapolation, if 6 parent/gp owns it in the linage, it caps off at 40%&nbsp;

**Summary of this section**

&nbsp;

The lowest chance of generating the gene is 20% for the basic version of any skill.

&nbsp;

All skills have a flat 5% chance of being a 3★, so it means you have a 95% chance to roll a 1-2 ★. However, you can increase the chance for 2★ and above with higher grades, explained later in the last section of this chapter.

# **Race genes**

&nbsp;

Winning G1 races in first place allows you to generate race genes, which provide different bonuses, such as stats, skills, or both.

Certain G1 races also grant skill hints when inherited. For example, the Queen Elizabeth Cup race gene grants both stats and the non-400m skill 非根幹距離.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Aoharu update: Aoharu scenario gene is a bit special.**

The Aoharu Scenario gene can still appear even if you&nbsp;  
1\. fail your Aoharu races.&nbsp;  
2\. Fail to complete the final URA portion of the run.

&nbsp;

Regarding the number of race factors generated at the end of the run, this is tied to the number of GI races won and mentioned during a magazine interview with the development staff.

&nbsp;

But whether they meant the total number of race factors OR if the particular G1 factor only appears if the G1 was run is unknown since Japanese is a very fickle language and could mean either. I’d assume they are just being vague and the race gene generation chances depend purely on luck (data below).

### **Race gene data**

The data below uses Satsuki-sho and Hopeful Stakes as comparisons to see if there are any differences in each race's chance of inheritance.

Source : Aoneko Uma’s data and NottinTV’s explanations [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WWKhpI3gQk0\&ab\_channel=NottinTV](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WWKhpI3gQk0&ab_channel=NottinTV)

![][image65]

The data shows that there is no bias in different G1 races, meaning all races will follow the  same gene proc rates.

Based on the data above you will have between 20% to 30% to inherit a G1/Race gene per run, with 5% chance for a 3★★★ version

&nbsp;

![][image66]

The data above is collected for Arima Kinen race genes, also comparing running 2 duplicate races vs 1\.

&nbsp;

**Reminder**: To generate a G1 race gene, you must have won the G1 race by coming in **First place.**

&nbsp;

For example, the Arima Kinen gene will **never** appear if you lost or didn't participate in Arima Kinen even if all 6 of your parents had the gene in their lineage.

&nbsp;

You only need to win any given G1 race once and there is no benefit for racing the same race again a second time, the odds of generation do not improve.

&nbsp;

Looking at a combination of all the above skill hints & race data, it's safe to say that all other race genes should follow the same formula. This would probably apply to the scenario genes too, but no indepth data has been collected on scenario gene rates.

# **Summarising the white gene generation rates**

### **Simplified linear interpretation** {#simplified-linear-interpretation}

|  | Min | Max | Approx bonus odds per lineage |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| White skills | 20% | 35% | \+2.5% |
| White skills ◎ | 25% | 40% | \+2.5% |
| Gold skills | 40% | 70% | \+5% |
| Race skills | 20% | 35% | \+2.5% |

&nbsp;

Simple explanation: having common genes in your lineage increases your odds of generating the gene.

### **Advanced explanation for the data purists**

Please take note that I’ve been treating the white skill generation rates as a linear growth function for ease of explanation and understanding for everyone thus far. However, aoneko\_uma has a different conclusion of the gene generation based on his data collection at [https://x.com/aoneko\_pochi/status/1775048834328195556](https://x.com/aoneko_pochi/status/1775048834328195556). The exponential relationship of this growth has also been confirmed with data obtained from Uma.moe & aya. N= 26,532,199 Team Trials Umas.

&nbsp;

While I’ve used the same min and max chances above to simplify the relationship, aoneko proposes that the additional chances per lineage follows an exponential growth instead.

![][image68]

&nbsp;

Gene generation probability \= **Base probability** × 1.1^(N)&nbsp;  
N \= Number of parents/grandparents possessing the target gene

The **base probability** would be the min chance as below

| White skills | 20% |
| :---- | :---- |
| White skills ◎ | 25% |
| Gold skills | 40% |
| Race skills | 20% |

White skills / White skills ◎ / Gold skills \- Cropped from the tweet

Therefore the expected per lineage jump in chances is tabled below.

![][image69]

&nbsp;

**More recent data confirmation (March 2026\)**

I’ve been consulting with Aya, who has also noticed the peculiarity and has gone forth to verify it using self collected data. You can read Aya’s findings in fuller detail on the matter linked here. [https://hakuraku.moe/notes/spark\_generation](https://hakuraku.moe/notes/spark_generation).&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Based on the independent data collected, Aya’s main concern with the simplified linear model I used is that they both overestimate low lineage and underestimate high lineage.

# **Uma grading and how it affects genes**

&nbsp;

Referenced source: [https://aoneko-uma.fanbox.cc/posts/4359075](https://aoneko-uma.fanbox.cc/posts/4359075)

After the introduction of Make a new track scenario in 2022, it had become possible for trainers to train Umas above the SS grade.

&nbsp;

It was here where we learnt that there was a hidden mechanic for how Uma grades affect the odds of gene generation.

Completing a run where your end grade is SS or above will increase the star QUALITY of your green/white genes.  Blue and Red genes are not affected by this mechanic and the chance of the particular genes appearing post run do not get boosted.

&nbsp;

**2023 data**&nbsp;

Source: [https://aoneko-uma.fanbox.cc/posts/3891258](https://aoneko-uma.fanbox.cc/posts/3891258)&nbsp;

In the above article, Aoneko investigates whether the new rating ceiling of UG/UF has any effect on white genes, and whether going above 1300 for stats affects blue genes.

~~Answer: **No**, the increased gene quality stops at SS grade for the Uma and SS for stats.~~  
**2024 Update**  
[https://twitter.com/aoneko\_pochi/status/1774676602628301180](https://vxtwitter.com/aoneko_pochi/status/1774676602628301180)

&nbsp;

Star vs End grade![][image71]Zoomed in graph (UF \-\> UE portion)![][image72]

Aoneko has discovered that ending your grade above UE has additional benefits to white gene generation, namely for 3\* Genes.

The gene quality chances be tabled as below

&nbsp;

| Chance of Stars for white genes | ★ | ★★ | ★★★ |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Below B | 90%&nbsp; | 10% | 0% |
| Below SS grade (less than 17500 score) | 50% | 45% | 5% |
| Above SS grade  , Below UE (More than 17500 score) | 20% | 70% | 10% |
| UE and Above&nbsp; | 17.5% | 70% | 12.5% |

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Jan 2025 update**: Ending the run at UB and above does not increase the rates any further. So UE is the current ceiling for boosted gene quality.

# **Chapter 5 : Recommended supergene mummy strategy**

&nbsp;

Combining the above Compatibility & Gene generation theories, Its time to aim for a high compatibility uma with stacked skills.

&nbsp;

Two examples are here: (Outdated screenshots from Early 2023\) [https://imgur.com/a/wfZaafj](https://imgur.com/a/wfZaafj)

&nbsp;

2024 Update: I’ve included a small snapshot for one example of what constitutes a strong parent. Order of importance, 3 Red \> good skills not found in your training deck \> 3 blue&nbsp;

![][image77]

![][image78]

As you can see above this Sirius was created for use in Mid distance & 差し/Betweener in mind.  
She lost Tennoushou Spring (lower compatibility with others who won it) and other g2 races(Doesn't matter)

&nbsp;

When building parents it would be best to follow this strategy of using the **same** support deck and running the **same races** as your parents for the following reasons.

&nbsp;

1\. The same support deck means you have access to buying up the same skills, which increases the chance of the same skills appearing in your run generation for up to 70% chance of the gene being generated.

2\.  Other than compatibility reasons, running the same races further leads to a higher chance of the common G1 genes being generated, allowing reinforcement of the genes, for up to 30% chance of passing it down.

As a reminder, there is no benefit for repeating any G1s that appear during the Classic or Senior years. Ie Arima Kinen on both years.

&nbsp;

**Do note:** you MUST win the G1 race or it will not be eligible for gene appearance  
Reccomendation: Do **NOT** learn unique skills passed down from inheritance if you do not need it to win races, this is just a waste of skill points since they do not lead to any skill gene generation. (More applicable to Umas pre MANT scenario as SP is extremely limited)

&nbsp;

It also helps to save your race preset so that you can consistently run the same races and don't run into a situation where you forget to run races or forget which races you've already ran.

&nbsp;

**When planning your gene farming runs**, consider between 2 philosophies, being a jack of all trades or specialising?

Will you **aim wide**, aiming for a wide versatile spread of different skills in your uma’s lineage?&nbsp;

Or will you **focus**, committing to the long and arduous grind of finding and reinforcing loops to create a parent with specific skill focuses and **3-star factors**?&nbsp;

Examples of both philosophies here.

Jack of all trades with many different skills vs URA essence skills specialist

# **Chapter 6: Red Gene deeper dive**

In this chapter we will be revisiting the Red Genes and diving a little deeper into strategies.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Take a look at the referenced uma musu station website if you wish to see the exact data.**

[**https://umamusustation.com/factor/red\_factor\_analysis.html**](https://umamusustation.com/factor/red_factor_analysis.html)

&nbsp;

Using the data provided by umamusu station, the probability of the red genes are **summarised** as follows.

* Aptitude must be A rank or higher in order for the gene to be generated.  
* Chance of Aptitude to be chosen as the Red Gene is selected at random, the chance is spread equally among aptitudes of A rank or higher  
* S rank does not increase the probability of the specific gene appearing.

&nbsp;

The gene rarity generated is fixed does not depend on the rank of aptitude chosen as the red factor, meaning S rank doesn't affect ☆ rates

・ 3 star ★★★ appearance rate is 10%

・ 2 star ★★☆ appearance rate is 70%

・ 1 star ★☆☆ appearance rate is 20%.

&nbsp;

This chart is a small snapshot of some of the uma museums in game.

Ideally you want to **reduce the RNG factor** for Red Gene selection by training someone with lesser native A stats

**Example 1:** Using Urara as an example if you are hunting for the Dirt gene, she only has 3 native A aptitudes, Sashi, Dirt and Short distance, as long as you do not raise any additional aptitude to A, you will have a good chance (33%) of generating a dirt red gene.

&nbsp;

**Example 2 :** Using a second example on the other side of the spectrum,

Mayano Top Gun has 5 A aptitudes and 2 Bs (sashi/oiko) or (betweener/chaser), carelessly raising these stats can potentially lead to a 7 way probability (17%) of inheriting a random red factor, ending up with a higher chance of an unwanted red gene.

# **Ideal strategy when farming specifically for red genes.**

Start off with a parent that has red genes neutral to your intended uma, ie. same red gene pool as your target daughter so it doesn't raise any additional unwanted B stat to A.

&nbsp;

Personal picks for the ideal uma to be used for parents (end of your loop, anything above will be referred as grandparent GP/GGP):

(Take in mind this section was created in 2021 during the Aoharu scenario, there are definitely better choices now and this section is extremely outdated)

&nbsp;

Mile: **Vodka/ Daiwa Scarlet** \- I like their unique skills

Mid/Long: **Maruzensky (Mid only)** The ideal acceleration for a ton of mid tracks.

**Symboli Rudolf** \- excellent compatibility and arguably the **best unique skill** to pass down for 先行/leader and further positions

Dirt: **Smart falcon** OR any of the B dirt umas (after you somehow get their dirt to A)

Unfortunately Urara has too poor compatibility to be recommended once better options appear

&nbsp;

**2022 update**

Accel ult parents are the meta parents for winning races and should be your focus since they are useful everywhere.

Classic examples are OG maruzensky, OG Seiun Sky / Dance Seiun Sky, Mejiro Ryan , Mejiro Dober, OG Kitasan Black / Kitasan White

**Obsolete older & once viable inherits:** ~~Other potential candidates, Meisho doto, gold city (Risky random ult), Monk El condor Pasa, Bridal Mayano Top Gun~~&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Here is my recommendation on the ideal priority list of Red genes for a parent.

&nbsp;

**1-2** Ground type genes \- Turf or Dirt \- because these are versatile to be used to parent for EVERY uma you train \- **S ground type** gives 5% bonus to **Power** stat.

**2-3** Distance type genes \- These allow you to focus on what distance you want to inherit \- **S Distance type** gives 5% bonus to **Speed** stat.

This is always a **major deciding factor** in winning any champions meeting, especially in longer distances, due to the length of the track.

&nbsp;

**I would not suggest more than 1** position related gene \- this is so you don't run into an accident in future parent runs like my Nige gene rudolf, a really bad choice for a parent since if you are parenting using rudolf, it is unlikely that your target character will be using nige strategy or want it to be in the inheritance pool.

Our JP bro has done his own research and summarised his findings on these sets of genes, I’m using his findings word for word translated, so when he says Awakening he just refers to all 3 types of the above genes.

 **Acquisition Conditions for Stat Genes:**

* The new awakening genes for Speed, Stamina, Power, Guts, and Wisdom are obtained by "successfully completing 12 or more trainings" of each respective stat.  
* Only "successful" Training counts are considered; failed training turns do not contribute.  
* Simultaneously acquiring three types of stat genes within 1 training run due to the limited number of turns is difficult, and realistically, aiming for two types is more feasible than three. Less or none if you are racing heavily.  
* In auto-training, focusing on two types of stats makes it easier to obtain the corresponding stat genes.

**Victory Conditions:**

* To obtain a directional gene (left or right turns) or seasonal (spring, summer, autumn, winter), you need to win at least **6 races** that meet the specific condition.  
  * Summer white only needs 5 additional races since the Debut race is ran in summer  
* This applies regardless of whether the race is a G1, OP, or any other type.  
* Total number of wins is irrelevant, it is about the number of wins under each specific condition.

**Seasonal Genes:**

* Spring, autumn, and winter genes are relatively easy to obtain due to the presence of fixed scenario races.  
* The summer factor is more challenging, as it requires careful planning of race schedules.  
* To get the summer awakening gene, you need to win 5 summer races outside of the debut race since the debut race is always in summer. This may be difficult to fit into a training schedule.

**Summer Race Considerations:**

* When aiming for the summer factor, consider including OP races in the junior season, as they tend to have lower chances of failure.  
* Other summer races include: JDD, Ibis SDx2, Late July through early September junior races, early September Classic/Senior races, and summer training camp races.

**Directional Genes:**

* If your umnya can run both dirt and turf races, or all distances on turf, you can likely obtain the left and right turn genes by participating in each G1 race once.  
* If the horse has limitations, you might need to run additional races.

**Key takeaway:**

* The key to getting the seasonal and directional awakening genes is to win at least six races that meet the specific conditions. Summer races are the most difficult to obtain.

# **Chapter 8: I’ve read all this, what do i do now?**

Strategic Gene Farming Decisions

&nbsp;

Before you even start a training run, plan your setup:

&nbsp;

* What is this parent used for? Ie. CM / LOH, GGP, GP, main parent?  
* Plan your parent route before starting any training run, identify the Umamusume with the right aptitude mix to generate the desired Red Genes.  
  * Eg. Can my uma generate Mid distance red gene?&nbsp;  
  * Do I have the parenting pass to lock a gene? Am I going to let RNG decide if I get an unwanted gene? (see end of chapter 6\)  
* Figure out your rental \- does it raise the aptitudes you need for your run? Ie. dirt, mile, mid.&nbsp;  
  * For example if you want to make a TM opera parent that is racing Dirt, mile, mid , long races. You will need to create your own parent with dirt/mile and rent another that can fulfill these conditions. C grade is usually the bare minimum to win a race with minimal difficulty.  
    For example using TMopera on the right, I had to make up for D apt on mile by buying up as many skills as I could.  
    &nbsp;  
  * **For global players and F2Ps who have no access to Gene passes.**  
    While you do want to raise dirt and mile for racing the maximum G1 races for compatibility, you will need to be careful not to accidentally raise unwanted aptitudes to A that will lower your chances during gene rolls.


  &nbsp;

  * Plan your support card deck to achieve the specific stat roll/skill pool you want for the run. Ie If you are looking for better odds of rolling stamina Blues \- U’d want at least a stamina card in the deck for higher odds. See below’s screenshot from U-tools (JP website only), they also have a great tool for planning your cards.  
    ![][image86]

&nbsp;

1. **Strategic Gene Prioritisation**

&nbsp;

Focus on the chance of generating the Red Genes first. These genes are the most crucial for upcoming competitive events (Champions Meeting, League of Heroes). For example, targeting for Turf inheritance can enable Smart Falcon to run turf events, or Mid-distance genes can boost Maruzensky's Mid-red proc rate (since she starts off at B Mid).

&nbsp;

Prioritisation Order for Red Genes: When farming Red Genes, always prioritise in this order: Distance \> Ground Type \> Strategy. Making your distance aptitude S is always the most critical for pvp events.

&nbsp;

The "S" Distance Advantage:

Achieving "S" rank in Distance is vital for competitive monthly race events. Without it, your Umamusume will be at a significant speed disadvantage against nearly every other opponent who had the foresight to prepare "S" Distance umas.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

2. **Plan your support card deck to push desired stats to the highest possible grade.**

&nbsp;

The "Chicken and Egg" Problem with Blue Genes:&nbsp;

While it's ideal to farm Blue Genes for stats which your deck lacks, this can be challenging if you don't already have strong support cards for those specific stats. I’d figure most players initially aim for 9-star blues as a target for their first parent.&nbsp;  
This means rolling a 3 star blue grandparent and then pairing it with a second uma with a 3 star blue, usually from rental Uma or another strong internal parent

The current favourite blue gene to have ~~for Design Your Island scenario is Guts.,~~ Speed/power for Onsen scenario.

For global, it will be Speed/Stamina/Power for a very long time, especially under URA/Aoharu/MANT

&nbsp;

3. **White Genes (Skills)**

Support cards: Plan your support cards to acquire relevant skills.&nbsp;

Internal parent / Rentals: You want to make parents or use rentals to hunt for skills normally unobtainable in your deck.

&nbsp;

4. **Compatibility**

Make sure your parent route has good compatibility with the Uma you wanted to train. Try to pair Classic crown racers with Classic crown, Tiara with Tiara routes. If you need to, use dirt races to bridge the compatibility gap.

Alternatively, LARC works as a smooth brained method to bridge the compatibility of short/mile umas with mid/long umas, Dirt & turf since the scenario naturally gives them natural turf  \+ Mid aptitude.&nbsp;

However, as the scenario is shortened and the total number of overlapping races is capped out at 16\. There is a hardcapped ceiling on the max compatibility. Very low skill points compared to current scenarios.

&nbsp;

For global (Pre-affinity rework): prioritise ◎ (Double Circle) Compatibility when pairing Umamusume. Use the in-game compatibility checker, or gametora’s compatibility tool for numbers to plan. To maximise compatibility, plan your parents to run the same overlapping races. Only G1, G2, and G3 races contribute to affinity before the rework; "OP" races do not count.

&nbsp;

To summarise the entire thing above

Set up a run / Fix your odds \-\> Spin the wheel \-\> Keep spinning till you get what you want.

# 

# **Key Takeaways for New Players:**

&nbsp;

Parenting is probably an optional choice, you can get by most content with minimally viable parents such as aligned red genes with peepeepoopoo Blue genes \+ 1 strong borrow.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

* Don't need to chase for perfect genes early. "Good enough"  is fine for your first batch of internal parents.&nbsp;  
* It's up to you how to define “Good enough”. Although personally. I think running a conflicting strategy parent with ZERO usable whites just because she has the red genes is **absolutely stupid**.&nbsp;  
  * You are better off just doing 1 run with a strong rental and accepting whatever gene that comes out than employing a parent with a lineage of completely conflicting strategy genes just solely for the red genes you want.  
  * This also applies to renting junk parents who have 100 white genes but only 10 of them are usable.

&nbsp;

Borrowing is your best friend. Always use ~~a strong~~ the strongest borrowable parent. If it's not in your follow list, make an effort to find it. [https://uma.pure-db.com/\#/search](https://uma.pure-db.com/#/search) (they have a global version too now, [https://uma-global.pure-db.com/\#/search](https://uma-global.pure-db.com/#/about) )

There's no excuse for renting a random junk parent when you only need 5 minutes or less to find a good parent, otherwise you’ll just end up wasting your own time building mediocre crap when instead, by borrowing 1 good parent, you will always end up with something that is good on 1 half of the parent linage.

&nbsp;

Blue Genes (stats) are great foundations for shoring up weak stats but CM specific white genes are more important now. Look to inherit and generate rare genes like Essence of stamina / **レースの真髄・体** which is unobtainable from cards.&nbsp;

(Shortly after writing this section, Speed Eishin flash and Power Fine motion exist with access to these.)

&nbsp;

Red Genes (aptitudes) are important for specific races. Focus on getting what your main Umamusume needs to run (e.g., Mile, Turf).  
Personally I think it's better to focus on getting your first 3 star red gene \+ preferably at least 2 Blue gene with the new aptitude genes  
Global: Prolly better off just getting your first 9 star blue \+ at least 2 star in Distance on main parent.

&nbsp;

White Skill Genes&nbsp;

These get more important as the game progresses and introduces more skills. There will be very strong speed/accel skills you would want to inherit for some PVP events.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

PVP events \- Champions meeting / League of Heroes / Monthly Matching *Beta version* (only existed for 1 month before being canned)  
PvE content doesn't really require using strong parents, maybe only Master challenges.&nbsp;

PvE refers to \- Stadium(Team Trials) / Legend races / Daily races / Master challenges.&nbsp;

# **Bonus Chapter: Inheritance chances\!**

12 August 2025 addition.

This is a bonus chapter because this guide was originally meant to only deal with Gene generation rates.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Huge credit goes to these 2 Japanese powerhouses; Polaris (@BourBon\_Polaris) and しょっぽ (@shoppo\_ura), who have spent a massive amount of time collating data on inheritance odds. Thanks DipstickPinez for sharing their tweet with me.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Polarisさん、しょっぽさん、もしこれを見ていたら──相性との関係を証明するために、たった一人で何千件ものデータポイントをまとめてくれたことに感謝します！

&nbsp;

Basically, they discovered that Cygames filed a patent for compatibility back in 2021 during the game’s initial launch. Shoppo surfaced it [here](https://x.com/shoppo_ura/status/1654582640941596673) and these 2 lads went to research if it held weight. Polaris's full testing data is can be found across his X (Twitter) and I won't be linking all of them as it's a whole boatload of data that he went to test using different game scenarios. Further, his data was collected very well with highly controlled settings so it can be trusted.

## **Effects of compatibility:**

Polaris started off his baseline with a bunch of tests using 0 compatibility Umas & also repeated the tests using Umas with some level of compatibility against the inheritance formula in the patent. Source: [https://x.com/BourBon\_Polaris/status/1819346545810235714](https://x.com/BourBon_Polaris/status/1819346545810235714)&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Polaris's tests showed results that were "roughly close" to predictions. Coincidentally he also remarked that the inheritance rate for grandparents is roughly half compared to the parent’s uma. This is just due to how GP compatibility is calculated at a lower weightage as compared to the parent Uma. Source: [https://x.com/BourBon\_Polaris/status/1846520715794882863](https://x.com/BourBon_Polaris/status/1846520715794882863)&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Just a snapshot of his inheritance [data](https://x.com/BourBon_Polaris/status/1862711283562553375/photo/4).

![][image87]

&nbsp;

In conclusion: The effects of compatibility have been proven to be the same throughout all scenarios and can be assumed to follow the formula below.&nbsp;

## **Inheritance formula:**

base\_inheritance\_odds\_per\_type \* (1 \+ individual\_compatibility\_score/ 100\) \= inheritance\_odds\_per\_type

3☆ Green Gene **example**: 15% \* (1 \+ 200/100) \-\> 15% \* (1 \+ 2\) \= 45%

*Reminder: Chapter 1 explains how individual compatibility is calculated.*

&nbsp;

Base proc rates (without compatibility)&nbsp;

| Gene type↓ / Base chance→ | ☆1 Rate | ☆2 Rate | ☆3 Rate |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Blue Stats&nbsp; | 70% | 80% | 90% |
| Red Genes & Aptitude whites (遺伝子) | 1% | 3% | 5% |
| Green (Unique Skill) | 5% | 10% | 15% |
| Race&nbsp; | 1% | 2% | 3% |
| Whites Skills, Scenario , Hidden whites  (目覚め& 隠し) | 3% | 6% | 9% |

The table is based on his data from 0 compatibility Umas.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Source is : [https://x.com/BourBon\_Polaris/status/1952727338547814695](https://x.com/BourBon_Polaris/status/1952727338547814695)

 ![][image88]![][image89]

In essence, he basically confirmed the individual inheritance theory at the same time while he was collecting these other data. Based on the formula above, you can see extremely high chances of your genes procc-ing for really high compatibility parents. If you want to maximise compatibility, you might want to consider adapting your parents to be able to do dirt races as well.

Further data verification&nbsp;

Source: [https://x.com/BourBon\_Polaris/status/1846520715794882863](https://x.com/BourBon_Polaris/status/1846520715794882863/photo/3)&nbsp;

He compared his expected values to the actual inheritances he achieved here with a 100 run sample set. This data confirms that inheritance rates for compatibility largely align with the theoretical formula, and any minor discrepancies can simply be attributed to the small sample size.

## **Inheritance-only Uma Musume / 継承専用ウマ娘**&nbsp; {#inheritance-only-uma-musume-/-継承専用ウマ娘}

**The official text is Inheritance, not legacies. Global localisation is bad \>:(**

&nbsp;

**Bulk Inheritance System**&nbsp;

\*Cygames understands how effective the “first hit is free” can be. Each player gets one set of 10 free tickets to test the new bulk inherit system post 5th Anniversary — so don’t burn it without proper planning.&nbsp;

This is a **PREMIUM** only feature. There is no indication any additional free tickets will be given out in the future, do let me know if your uncle works at cygames and if there will be.![][image98]

&nbsp;

Note that the bulk inheritance works on its own rules and none of any of the content in my guide above can be used for the bulk inheritance plan. However, if you rent/use any inheritance-only uma for **STANDARD** parenting, the usual genes generation/acquisition rules apply for the next generation of umas.  
&nbsp;

### **How the inheritance planning works:**

&nbsp;

Before you dive in, see that button just before you start your bulk inheritance? That’s the **Trainer Guide**, which most players have been ignoring like a "Terms of Service" pop-up.

Cygames stealthily added some fine print to the help page on **27 February 2026**, regarding this feature. When enabled, all recommended hints for the selected PVP event will actually have **enhanced chances** to appear as factors on your inheritance-only Umas.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Inheritance-only Click™ Remote instruction manual.**

&nbsp;

1. Create a Plan, up to 5 can be saved  
2. Choose a training scenario  
3. Pick an Uma  
4. Set up the parents you are renting  
   * Using a friend's inheritance-only Uma Musume will not consume rentals nor money.  
5. Plan your race rotation settings for the Uma Musume to be acquired in bulk  
   * The win rate for a race is calculated based on the aptitude of the target Uma Musume. (Patched on May 20\) ~~and their trophy acquisition status.~~  
   * If the distance and ground aptitude is A, the base win rate will be **110%.**  
   * If the distance and ground aptitude is B or lower, the win rate will be reduced according to the suitability. (no rates declared by Cygames)  
   * If you have raced for three or more consecutive turns, your win rate will be reduced.  
   * The more consecutive turns a uma races, the greater the reduction in its win rate.  
6. Set up to 10 prioritised genes&nbsp;  
   * The chances of the skill genes appearing depends on your support card’s limit break. The higher the LB the better. No rates known yet.  
   * However, genes from parent lineage can too be selected. \~5% chance.  
   * Turning the training guide to \[ON\] **extra**\-increases your chances of these **SUPER** \- recommended genes appearing. Rates are 1.1x.  
   * Sample screenshot of **SUPER** recommended genes based on the tracks.![][image99]  
   * Rental decks are not allowed.  
7. If you have the Factor lock or combined parenting pass, you get to pick the gene to lock when generating parents.  
   * Blue genes: Unknown how its determined  
   * Red Genes: Same random pick among all the A aptitudes  
8. Execute Bulk Acquisition via the Click™ remote for high-speed breeding.![][image100]  
9. Cry because the rolls and the fast forwarded experience was bad anyway, just like in the movie.

&nbsp;

**17 July update**

&nbsp;

Shoppo also investigated win rate reduction for running consecutive races @&nbsp;  
[https://x.com/shoppo\_ura/status/2077988949495279684?s=20](https://x.com/shoppo_ura/status/2077988949495279684?s=20)&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Essentially aptitudes for ground and distance have the same weightage. Meaning AG \= GA \= DD

**Patched out on May 20 2026**&nbsp;

  * ~~Trophies cannot be earned by Umas created in this mode and you are advised to do at least ONE normal run with the Uma to win the races you are planning to send them on.~~  
    1. ~~If aptitudes are at A, you will have a base win rate of 110%~~

&nbsp;

**Other stuff**

Inheritance only uma cannot be used for additional contents that require you to send an Uma to race, such as daily races, legend races etc.

&nbsp;

All the above data has been obtained from Cygames’ official website. [https://www.games.umamusume.jp/\#/help?p=3](https://www.games.umamusume.jp/#/help?p=3)
