#### **Uma Plan users**

Since this feature launched alongside the current scenario, a new automation setting is available. To manually select your re-rolled inheritance during auto-runs, you must check the "Pause at the inheritance turn" box. Otherwise, auto-kun will automatically select the inheritance for you.

![][image101]

#### Other notes:

We all currently know that the [**Breeder’s Cup Scenario**](#breeders-cup-scenario-[auto-enabled]) that was released together with this system is an absolute dumpster fire for parenting. However, if you use this **Bulk Inheritance** tool specifically for the BC scenario, you actually end up with better results than both auto *and* manual play.

Here is the breakdown of why this is stronger:

* **The SP Gap:** Under a standard BC scenario auto-run, your runs usually end with a measly **4–6k** skill points.&nbsp;  
  * Whereas you already get a stable 5-6k in DYI or 6-7k in Onsen.  
* **The Skill Pool:** Realistically, you’re rolling for **30–50 skills** worth of inheritance factors with grades ranging from **UF to UD. (**You’d want a minimum of UE grades.)  
* **The Efficiency Fix:** By using **Mass Inheritance**, you’ll net more factors from bulk inheritance than you ever could as compared to an auto or manual run (for BC).  
* **Deck flexibility** : I’ve heard mentions that you can ignore scenario friend cards to run 6 stat cards instead and from my own testing it looks like the case.

Essentially, Cygames did a “create a problem and sell the fix” to deal with the miserable farmability of the BC scenario.

Shoppo summarised his findings here. Tweet thread linked here: [https://x.com/shoppo\_ura/status/2033476508719956453](https://x.com/shoppo_ura/status/2033476508719956453)&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Gene appearance rates**

Arranging the results by groups of priority, rare (Gold skill), Trainer guide, and inheritance. The results are quite close to the expected values of a normal run.

![][image104]

&nbsp;

Race factors, awakening, and hidden factors are also within the expected range.

![][image105]![][image106]

Just like a normal parenting run, the base acquisition rate is 20% plus the standard bonus from the common genes in your uma’s lineage.

When it comes to races, even if you win the Arima Kinen twice or win 18 right-handed races, the gene acquisition rate doesn't double or triple. This is in-line with expectations.

&nbsp;

**Scenario gene:**

He found that the Onsen scenario factor seems to be around 40% appearance rate, but it is a mystery as the expected value of scenario factor up till the Island scenario was supposed to be around 30%.

&nbsp;

He can’t tell if it's because the hot spring resort has a higher acquisition rate or if it was a bonus specifically for the designated uma, or just a lucky streak?

&nbsp;

**★ Rarity of genes**

The star rate for priority factors is the upper end of the rates. (UE and above)&nbsp;

&nbsp;

★3:★2:★1 \= 10%:70%:20%

&nbsp;

According to the help section of the Inheritance-only, these seem to depend on support cards, but in his tests, all support cards were fully enhanced SSR and had the same star rate, so hes wondering if this is the maximum tier of rates?

&nbsp;

So he tested and significantly reduced the support card power and noted that his white rarity rates were following the SS to UF banding.

★3:★2:★1 \= 5%:45%:50% was used.

![][image107]

My take is: Don’t use too scuffed a deck with too many low LBs. The hidden end grade of the inheritance-only uma is likely following what your deck might produce in an Auto run on the chosen scenario.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

For reference these are the Upper, middle, lower bands he refers to. Not particularly sure what these S to F ranks are referring to.

![][image108]

&nbsp;

Extra reading: [https://x.com/shoppo\_ura/status/2034940511891640497](https://x.com/shoppo_ura/status/2034940511891640497)&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Shoppo expands more on his data collected and how setting a priority skill affects the simulation of your inheritance only runs. His uma setup here:&nbsp;

[https://x.com/shoppo\_ura/status/2029781499952890241](https://x.com/shoppo_ura/status/2029781499952890241)&nbsp;

&nbsp;

It’s a lot to go through but here’s something interesting.

###  **Sources of Factors**

* **Inheritance Skills:** Skills gained solely through inheritance (not from the training Uma, Support Cards, or scenario hints) showed a consistent acquisition rate of about **5%**.  
* **Race Factors:** Factors like "Nakayama Racecourse" or "Non-Core Distance" appeared even without hints or inheritance, likely originating from the race results themselves.  
* **Scenario Links:** Simply having a Scenario Link Support Card (e.g., Mihono Bourbon) does not mean all its skills are automatically prioritised for factor generation.

# **Final Summary: I don't want to read, just give me the numbers**&nbsp;

![][image111]

\-[Aoneko Uma’s twitter](https://x.com/aoneko_pochi/status/1762370579603304731?s=20)

**Blue Genes**&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Highest chance of getting ★★★ for your target stat after a run (SS or higher stat): (10% \* 20%) \= 2%

Lowest chances of getting ★★★ for your target stat after a run (B stat): (5% \* 20%) \= 1%

&nbsp;

**Blue Gene farm strategy**

In scenarios before MANT, you will need to use strong support cards, plan for good training bonuses & high Speciality rate/tokui cards in your run with an aim of at least 600 (B) in your target stat. After LARC: Unga bunga lol

**Red farm Strategy**

Equally random chance to be rolled among all your A and above aptitudes, some Uma are worse off in trying to roll your intended gene since they have more A aptitudes.

・ 3 star ★★★ appearance rate is 10%

・ 2 star ★★☆ appearance rate is 70%

・ 1 star ★☆☆ appearance rate is 20%.

&nbsp;

Don't raise proficiencies that you do not want to rank A

**Green Genes farming strategy**

The gene generation chances follow the same principle as white genes, thanks Aya\!

&nbsp;

| Rank score band | Samples | 1-star | 2-star | 3-star |
| :---: | ----: | ----: | ----: | ----: |
| 1000 \<= score \< 6500 | 1,546,921 | 89.99% | 10.01% | 0.00% |
| 6500 \<= score \< 17500 | 14,274,987 | 49.97% | 45.01% | 5.02% |
| score \>= 17500 | 460,910 | 19.94% | 70.05% | 10.00% |

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Race genes/White skills explained**&nbsp;

You have between 20% to 30% chance to inherit a G1 race gene per run. (And you must win that particular G1 Race too)

White skill chance of inheritance: \[20-30% / 40-70%\]    \[White skill/Gold skill\]

All white skills have a flat 5% chance of being a 3★, so it means a 95% chance to be 1-2 ★  
This % is doubled if your uma’s grade is SS and above, increases further if you end at UE and above.

&nbsp;

| Chance of Stars for white genes | ★ | ★★ | ★★★ |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Below B | 90%&nbsp; | 10% | 0% |
| Below SS grade (less than 17500 score) | 50% | 45% | 5% |
| Above SS grade  , Below UE (More than 17500 score) | 20% | 70% | 10% |
| UE and Above&nbsp; | 17.5% | 70% | 12.5% |

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Race genes/White skills farming strategy**

Having the same white gene in your parentage increases the chance of receiving the same white gene & you must also learn the respective skill AND win the same race if you want it to appear.&nbsp;

**4th Anniversary new White genes**  
The chapter is already as miniaturised as possible, go [read it](#bookmark=id.wq6crmup1d80).&nbsp;

**Effects of compatibility on parents:**

Higher compatibility raises the odds of inheriting genes from said lineage.

&nbsp;

For the best compatibility overlap all the races you can, raise dirt aptitude for dirt races increased compatibility and/or bridging other rotations.

\-Dirt rotations are not for you Global gremlins. yet

**Conclusion**: At the end of the day it's up to you as to how greedy you are for genes, what you wish to target for your ideal breeding parent and what combination of strategies you use in training/picking choices.

It is in your best interest to plan your red genes early before you commit to any farming strategy, otherwise 1 bad red gene can potentially ruin your perfect parent (look at my [early Rudolf](#example-of-a-failed/bad-red-inheritance) for example)&nbsp;

&nbsp;

"All it takes is one bad ~~day~~ Gene to reduce the sanest man alive to lunacy. That's how far the world is from where I am. Just one bad ~~day~~ gene.”

&nbsp;

\-Joker, Batman: The killing joke "
